title: ID Churn Sentinel registry changelog v1
description: What the registry watched, and how that changed. Derived from two committed revisions of sources/registry.json by `sentinel registry changelog`; never hand-written. Every event says what the registry said on either side of a revision pair. No event makes a claim about the page at the URL, and none makes a claim about the law.

unrecorded_before.description: Where recorded history begins. Reconstructing events from revisions predating this schema is out of scope, so the alternative to this block is a log whose earliest entry reads as the registry's first change. `revision` is the sha256 of the canonical registry at the point the log was opened.

kind.description: The closed vocabulary. A consumer may branch exhaustively on this field. `verification_expired` means the entry stopped being human-verified between the two revisions; it does NOT assert that a recheck date had passed, because a diff of two files has no clock to evaluate one against. The recorded recheck date travels in `expires_at` so a reader can judge for themselves. A named human finding a page is NOT the official one is `verification_rejected`, never an expiry.

subject_id.description: A registry source id, or `gap:<JURISDICTION>:<document_class>` for a gap, which the registry does not itself carry an id for. Source ids cannot contain a colon, so the two spaces cannot collide.

from.description: The earlier value, when the kind has one. OMITTED, never blank: a blank would read as a value of "".

to.description: The later value, when the kind has one.

reason.description: Why a gap exists, drawn from the registry's closed gap vocabulary. Never free text, and never an operator note.

actor.description: The named human whose decision this event records — a verifier, or the reviewer of a fetch policy. Absent for events no person authored.
